# PresetPicker

Presets as cards, where choosing one applies it at once. Each card (a layout, a template, a mode) has a name, a line about it and an optional tag. The preset in use is marked "In use" and `aria-current`. The arrow keys, Home and End move focus between the cards without choosing (right to left, the left arrow moves to the next card), and Enter, Space or a click chooses. Choosing the preset already in use does nothing.

```tsx
import { PresetPicker } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/preset-picker/preset-picker";
```

## Example

```tsx
<PresetPicker label="Start from a layout" items={presets} value={layout} onValueChange={useLayout} />
```

## Use instead when

- Use `ChoiceCard` instead for a choice a form submits later (arrow keys there change the choice), and `SegmentedControl` for a few short options without descriptions.

## Props

Type: `PresetPickerProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: width, margins, grid placement (`mt-4`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `currentLabel` | `string` | `"In use"` | The mark on the preset in use, for other languages. |
| `items` (required) | `readonly PresetPickerItem[]` |  | The presets, in the order they show. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | What is being chosen, for screen readers ("Start from a layout"). Required, so the list has a name. |
| `onValueChange` (required) | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called with a preset's value when the person chooses one that is not in use. It applies at once. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |
| `value` | `string \| null` |  | The preset in use. Its card is marked "In use" and `aria-current`. |

## Native attributes

Also accepts the attributes in React's `HTMLAttributes` (`id`, `aria-*`, event handlers), passed to the rendered element, except those named on this page.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `current`: Not a prop. The preset in use is `value`: `<PresetPicker value={current}>`.
- `onSelect`: Not a prop. Choosing calls `onValueChange`: `<PresetPicker onValueChange={(value) => use(value)}>`.
- `options`: Not a prop. The presets are `items`: `<PresetPicker items={presets}>`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: PresetPicker merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with its own replaces it.[^layout-classes]

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `PresetPickerItem`

One preset in a `PresetPicker`.

```ts
interface PresetPickerItem {
  /** Identifies the preset; `onValueChange` receives it. */
  value: string;
  /** The preset's name ("Chats first"). */
  label: string;
  /** One line about what it is for or what it holds. */
  description?: ReactNode;
  /** A small mark after the name, such as "Saved" or "New". */
  tag?: string | undefined;
}
```
